claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The Open Semantic Interchange is a vendor-neutral YAML standard for writing semantic definitions such as measures, dimensions and metadata, intended to make definitions portable between tools; its v1.0 spec shipped 27 January 2026 under Apache 2.0, and it entered the Apache Incubator as Apache Ossie in June 2026 with more than 50 backers.
claims.quote: The OSI v1.0 spec was released on 27 January 2026 under Apache 2.0, and the project entered the Apache Incubator in June 2026. More than 50 organizations back it.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: OSI defines meaning only: it has no execution engine, and its v1.0 core does not codify access policy as a first-class element.
claims.quote: OSI has no execution engine, and its v1.0 core does not codify access policy.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A semantic execution layer is distinguished from an interchange format: a format carries definitions, while an execution engine resolves requests into queries, proves join paths, applies row/column policy and emits dialect-specific SQL.
claims.quote: Something has to resolve the request into a query. Something has to choose the correct join path and prove it is valid. Something has to apply the row-level rule that hides the other regions. Something has to emit SQL in the exact dialect of the target engine.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A definition, regardless of how it is authored, must land in a typed semantic graph before it can be executed; from there the layer adds compile-time RBAC/ABAC and row/column predicates so filtered rows are never read.
claims.quote: The definition, however it is written, still has to land in a typed semantic graph before it can be executed.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The proposed runtime pipeline for a governed semantic layer is: intent, then context resolution, then constrained planning, then governed execution; it claims one graph compiles to the exact SQL of 16+ engines with point-in-time reproducibility.
claims.quote: The runtime is one line: intent → context resolution → constrained planning → governed execution.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The source's stated position is that a well-governed semantic layer that understands business context yields more reliable AI-driven analytics than fine-tuning the model itself.
claims.quote: A well-governed semantic layer that understands business context creates more reliable AI-driven analytics than fine-tuning the model itself.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Adoption of the interchange standard is shallow in practice: many of the 50-plus backers have joined but fewer ship a lossless production reader/writer, with broad phase-2 adoption framed as the 2026 test and de-facto-standard status targeted for 2027.
claims.quote: Many of the 50-plus organizations have signed on. Fewer have shipped a production reader and writer that round-trips real definitions without loss.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Converters bridging existing tool formats into OSI had been merged for dbt MetricFlow, GoodData, Salesforce and Apache Polaris, which is how portability starts to become concrete.
claims.quote: There are converters for dbt MetricFlow, GoodData, Salesforce, and Apache Polaris.
